title: Openness Scope & Enterprise Asset Protection
subtitle: A protocol that standardizes non-competitive domains so organizations focus on what differentiates them
philosophyLead: OpenOrgOS does not aim to take away an organization's competitive advantage.
philosophyGoal: We provide the common protocol for verifiable exchange across organizational boundaries. Business logic, legal interpretation, and organizational behavior are delegated to national or domain-specific committees.
standardizeIntro: For protocol extensions common across many inter-organizational relationships (identity exchange, authority delegation, audit linkage, and similar), we encourage modularizing and returning them to the community where possible. These are shared infrastructure for inter-organizational communication — not sources of competitive advantage.
nonStandardizeTitle: Domains we do not aim to standardize
nonStandardizeIntro: Assets that define company-specific competitive advantage should stay separate from OpenOrgOS and be managed by each company. OpenOrgOS never requires sharing or publishing them.
privateModuleIntro: Modules built on OpenOrgOS do not have to be public. Companies may freely combine:
privateModuleNote: OpenOrgOS welcomes returning good modules to the community but does not require it.
principlesNot: OpenOrgOS does not aim to share competitive domains.
principlesYes: We aim for a world where non-competitive domains are shared so each company can focus on its true competitive edge.
messageLead: Adopting OpenOrgOS does not make every company the same.
messageSame: Only the protocol foundation is commonized. What defines organizational value remains protected:
messageBody: OpenOrgOS does not strip away what makes your company unique.
messageClosing: It is the foundation that lets you concentrate on the domains where uniqueness matters.
taglineNot: OpenOrgOS is not an internal operations OS to standardize competitive domains.
taglineYes: OpenOrgOS is a global protocol to standardize non-competitive inter-organizational domains and focus resources on competitive ones.
